title: fix: show why plugin state access fails after an update
body:
Refs #156930. Thanks @Fuma2013 for the report and the restart/foreground control evidence.

## What Problem This Solves

Plugin-state failures appear in structured logs without their nested cause or the process that captured them, hiding why an older background reader rejects an upgraded database.

## User Impact

Structured records now include bounded nested causes, native error codes/errno, and the capturing process ID, thread ID, and OpenClaw version. Operators can distinguish a schema-version refusal from a file-open failure. Existing credential redaction remains active; arbitrary error properties and stacks are excluded.

For the reported 9.5 companion / 9.6 Gateway skew, update and relaunch OpenClaw.app; a Gateway-only restart leaves the old app worker in place. The diagnostics change must ship in the next npm release; the separate macOS-only rebuild cannot update the installed CLI/Gateway package.

## Why This Change Was Made

The tagged 9.5 app selects its signed private Node/OpenClaw payload, validates that payload against the app's version and build, and runs `node worker`; updating the external npm CLI does not replace it. The node-host plugin registry registers the same Codex catalog commands and keyed-state store. Its resident catalog reconciles every 30 seconds against the same profile's shared state database. Tagged 9.5 supports schema 17 and rechecks schema support even when reusing a read handle; 9.6 migrates the shared database to schema 18.

This establishes a version-skew mechanism consistent with a failing app-owned background reader, successful 9.6 foreground reads, and persistence across Gateway-only restarts. We have not captured the reporter's exact failing PID or nested cause, so this PR references the issue rather than claiming that attribution is independently proven.

The fix belongs to the plugin-state error and transport owners. One shared bounded cause serializer serves both worker transport and JSON logs; the existing canonical codec preserves typed/aggregate errors and now carries `errno`. JSON uses `errorCode` for native causes so OAuth-code redaction does not hide them; in-memory `.code` is unchanged. `owner` identifies where the plugin-state error was constructed, including the caller thread for pre-dispatch failures. No schema, migration, retention, or admission-policy changes.

<details>
<summary>Tagged source evidence</summary>

- [Packaged app selects its private worker](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.9.5/apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/CommandResolver.swift#L257), and [validates the matching private payload](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.9.5/apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/NodeMode/BundledNodeWorker.swift#L21).
- [Codex registration binds resident state and node commands](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.9.5/extensions/codex/index.ts#L190); [node catalog dispatch](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.9.5/extensions/codex/src/session-catalog-listing.ts#L64) reaches that catalog.
- [Gateway disconnection only retires the connection](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.9.5/src/node-host/worker.ts#L98); a distinct stop message closes the app-owned runtime.
- [Resident reconciliation runs every 30 seconds](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.9.5/extensions/codex/src/session-catalog-currency.ts#L22).
- [Reused read handles still validate schema support](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.9.5/src/state/openclaw-state-db-readonly.ts#L223); [plugin state wraps admission failures as OPEN_FAILED](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.9.5/src/plugin-state/plugin-state-store.sqlite.ts#L148).
- Release `eb377ac` predates both #156643 and #156824, so their specific admitted-facts regression is excluded. It also predates #156400 and #156387; neither changes this tagged Codex path.

</details>

## Evidence

- Published npm 2026.9.5 → 2026.9.6, isolated Linux/Node 24.19 state and free ports: a 5,761-entry resident namespace migrated from schema 17 to 18; the 9.6 Gateway catalog, synchronous/asynchronous SDK reads, and native-rollout reconciliation succeeded. `quick_check=ok`; no background warning appeared during 65 seconds after readiness or the subsequent native-rollout restart probe.
- The 9.5 SDK reading that same migrated store produced `PLUGIN_STATE_OPEN_FAILED`, operation `entries`, with nested `SqliteSchemaVersionError`: database schema 18, reader supports 17. This was an isolated reader reproduction, not a live capture of the reporter's macOS process.
- Logging regressions failed before the fix. They exercise the real JSONL sink after worker capture/restore, native and canonical causes, cyclic aggregates, owner preservation, and bearer-token redaction. Focused run: 20/20 tests; approximately 165 ms test time, 30.02 s wrapper wall including 18.84 s compiler preparation. The existing real-worker error test also checks that worker identity survives restoration.
- Committed-head importer selection: 14 Vitest shards passed in 608.40 s, with 77 files producing passing-test records. The two Gateway close suites omitted by multi-project selection then passed explicitly in the supported aggregate configuration: 85 tests, 23.76 s. The opt-in external live suite was not enabled. `pnpm build` exited 0 in 306.72 s; its UI report flagged a Mermaid gzip budget overage (1,555.8 KiB versus 960.0 KiB), not investigated in this lane. Fresh `autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main` found no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Pre-existing test performance is assigned to a separate follow-up: `canonical-descendant.integration.test.ts` passed 73 cases in 182.587 s of test time; the first `server.codex-failure-recovery.test.ts` case took 37.121 s. Both timing issues predate this change and are being handled in a separate performance follow-up. No tests were weakened, skipped, or retiered for this change.
- Final committed-head `check:changed` passed on Testbox (exit 0, 25m 41.568s), including core types, all 25 core-test typecheck graphs, formatting, lint, schema/ownership guards, and zero runtime import cycles.
- Production +115/−72 (net +43); tests +85/−1; docs +13/−2. The shared helper replaces the duplicated cause scanner.
